newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche's Kopper sees huge changes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Kopper sees huge changes - paper.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG chairman Hilmar Kopper, who steps down from the job next week, foresees huge changes being unleashed on Europe's banking and financial markets as a result of the planned single currency, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

"My imagination is not big enough to grasp all the possible changes that will occur," he told the newspaper in an interview. "It will be so interesting that sometimes I regret I don't have a few more years here".
After seven years as chairman Kopper will be succeeded after next Tuesday's annual meeting by Rolf Breuer. Kopper will head the non-executive supervisory board, a role he calls "advisory".
Kopper said Deutsche Bank would have to adapt, under Breuer's chairmanship, to a rapidly changing environment.

In Germany there had to be a further rationalisation of the public sector savings and cooperative banks. "We need a streamlining process. This country is over-branched and over-banked, so something has to happen," Kopper told the newspaper.

The competitive pressures and challenges of the single currency would lead to big markets in cross-border securities, money and asset management. "The euro will decide, it will exert much stronger pressure over who does what with whom."
He ruled out, however, an immediate shake-up of Germany's big commercial banks.
From a strong financial base, Deutsche Bank intended to continue expanding across Europe as well as in North America and the Asia-Pacific Region, Kopper said.
